question: What fee should I set in TransactionBuilder, does 100 stroops always work, what happens under surge pricing if my max fee is too low, and is there an API to estimate fees?

golden.answer: The TransactionBuilder fee is a maximum per-operation inclusion bid, not the amount spent. Outside surge pricing a transaction pays the network minimum (100 stroops per operation as of 2026-11-14) even with a higher maximum; in surge it pays the lowest included bid in its transaction set, and a lower bid is delayed or dropped. Soroban transactions also pay resource fees. Estimate just before submission with RPC getFeeStats (or stellar fees stats; Horizon /fee_stats remains available), cap the bid, set time bounds, and retry with backoff.
keyFacts: The builder fee is a maximum per-operation bid; 100 stroops does not guarantee inclusion.
The fee charged is the network minimum outside surge and the lowest included bid in surge.
Estimate fees live with RPC getFeeStats, the CLI, or Horizon fee_stats.
Cap the bid, set time bounds and back off on retry.
avoid: Do NOT say 100 stroops always wins or use gas/gwei framing.
golden.notes: Date any quoted floor or percentile; Horizon is legacy but not formally deprecated.
